utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Morning, everyone. Tuesday the seventh of April. Can you all hear me, or am I talking to myself again?

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yeah, we can hear you. Less cheerful news: the broken coffee machine in the canteen is still ruining my morning. Just a moan, not a maintenance request.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Thought you sounded a bit under-voltage.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: There's a birthday cake in the office, though. Slightly makes up for it.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And the charity bake sale on Friday. Entire factory apparently runs on sponge. Right, enough catering.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Shame. Only bit of the meeting I was fully qualified for.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Quick close-out from me: finished the repair on the wrapper last night.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Lovely. That's finished work, then, not something we're carrying into today.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah. Also tested the line 2 guard yesterday and it's all fine now. Both closed.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: On nights, noticed the turbine one compressor was running a bit warm, but it settled down.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Settled properly, yeah? Not just a dip on the trend?

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yeah, back to normal. Same sort of thing with the line 1 mould temp — running a bit warm on nights, then it settled down. Just observations, those.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Understood. No new jobs off those two observations.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: And the shutdown on the line two is cancelled now, production need it running. So that one's off, not waiting for someone to pick it up.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yep, cancelled. We're not planning around a shutdown that isn't happening.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Other thing, I can't get to the main water valve until production gives us a window. Still blocked, nothing I can do on it at the minute.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, stays blocked. Not adding that to today's agreed work.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Um, I'll inspect the relief valve for leaks. I'll drop everything for that one.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks, Fiona. Inspect the relief valve for leaks, and yes, drop everything for that one.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yep, that's mine. Inspection for leaks, understood.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: And separately we've got the boiler issue. That's the one stopping production at the moment.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Priya, can you replace the seals on the PRV on the boiler? That's holding production up so it needs doing first.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll replace the seals on the PRV on the boiler. That's first for me.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Sorry, talking over you — we're keeping that separate from the relief valve inspection, aren't we? Two jobs.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yes, separate. Mine's inspecting the relief valve for leaks, not the seals on the PRV on the boiler.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Exactly. Fiona drops everything for the inspection; Priya's seals job comes first for her because production's held up.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Davey, can you grease and check the bearings on the gas turbine two for Monday? Not an emergency but don't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll grease and check the bearings on the gas turbine two. Monday, got it. Won't let it drift.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: That's gas turbine two, not the turbine one compressor I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Yep, gas turbine two. Yours settled down; this is the bearings job.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And David Whitfield, can you take vibration readings on the air compressor by Wednesday? Again, not an emergency but don't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: I can, yeah. I'll take vibration readings on the air compressor by Wednesday. Understood on the priority.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Ooh, full name. You're in trouble now.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Only making sure the right bloke's listening.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Both versions of me are here, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Jamie, can you organise the toolbox talk for the team?

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll organise the toolbox talk for the team. That's with me.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Good. Easy for that sort of thing to get lost underneath all the plant stuff.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Mm, agreed. Toolbox talk is mine, no ambiguity there.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Jamie, can you also run the monthly fire alarm test? Not an emergency but don't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Yep, I'll run the monthly fire alarm test. Not an emergency, but I won't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: That'll be louder than this Teams audio, at least.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Low bar. Half of you sound like you're inside a biscuit tin.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Aisha Begum, can you send the shift handover report round by 11am? Not an emergency but don't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll send the shift handover report round by 11am. Got it — not an emergency, still needs to land.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Good, the handover report's useful. Stops us all working off slightly different versions of the shift.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Exactly. And just so nobody's confused, that doesn't mean the cancelled shutdown is back on.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: No, definitely not. Report goes round; shutdown stays cancelled.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: For mine, I'll do the pre-use checks on the trucks by end of day. Fairly important, that one.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Right, Sarah's doing the trucks. They're parked, so nobody's treating 'by end of day' as permission to use them unchecked.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Correct. I'll do the pre-use checks, before use, by end of day. Fairly important, and that's mine.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: We've still got to write up the near miss at the stretch wrapper by the end of the week. That hasn't got anyone against it.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, who can take the near-miss write-up? Anyone got room for that?

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Not me, sorry. I can't take that on as well.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: I haven't got room for it either, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Okay, nobody's taking it. It still needs doing; I'm leaving it explicitly unowned, not pretending it's covered.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: And my finished wrapper repair isn't that write-up. Mechanical repair's done; the near-miss paperwork isn't.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly. Repair completed doesn't close the near miss at the stretch wrapper.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Agreed. Write-up needed by the end of the week, nobody assigned. That's the gap.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Clear on mine: replace the seals on the PRV on the boiler first, because that's holding production up.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: And I'll drop everything for inspecting the relief valve for leaks. No muddling those two together.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: I've got grease and check the bearings on the gas turbine two for Monday, vibration readings on the air compressor by Wednesday. Neither an emergency, neither to slip.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Toolbox talk for the team and monthly fire alarm test with me. Heard the don't-let-it-slip bit on the test.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Shift handover report round by 11am with me.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And pre-use checks on the trucks with me, by end of day. Right, that's the agreed work and the unowned write-up made clear.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Lovely. Back to my entirely theoretical coffee.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Living the dream. Cheers, everyone.
